# Time series {#sec-time-series}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

library(rebook)
chapterPreamble()
```

Microbial communities are dynamic, constantly evolving over time. However,
despite temporal fluctuations driven by environmental and other factors, the
microbiome retains its core characteristics [@Schmidt2018].

Cross-sectional studies capture the microbiome at a single time point. In
contrast, longitudinal (temporal) study designs follow the same individuals
over time. This allows researchers to study how microbial communities change,
for example, in response to an intervention such as antibiotic or probiotic
treatment, or during the progression of a disease.

Longitudinal data also help to interpret cross-sectional findings. A single
sample reflects not only differences between individuals but also the natural
day-to-day variability within each individual's microbiome. By sampling the
same subjects repeatedly, this within-subject variability can be estimated and
separated from between-subject differences. This reduces the uncertainty in
comparisons between groups.

Analyzing longitudinal data includes aspects that need to be taken into
account, such as the dependence between samples collected from the same
subject.

Most of the methods introduced earlier in this book can be applied to
longitudinal data with small modifications. For more details, see the
following chapters:

- [@sec-time-diversity]
